messages:
sam: hitting a parity/typing annoyance in the python SDK async client. when server returns a non-json error body we end up surfacing a JSON parse ValueError instead of a typed ApiError. users can't reliably read status_code or request_id in exception handlers.

sam: minimal repro (async):
async with AsyncClient(key) as c:
    await c.create("bad")

server replied 400 text/html and the stack shows ValueError from resp.json().

julia: ugh. this leaks implementation details. SDK should always raise ApiError for 4xx/5xx with typed attrs so mypy users can access them.

maria: agree. suggested ApiError public surface: status_code: int, headers: Dict[str, str], raw_body: str, parsed: Optional[Dict[str, Any]], request_id: Optional[str]. Put these in the py.typed/stubs so static checkers see them. Also preserve __cause__ when re-raising so traceback still shows original parse error if helpful.

sam: small fix idea: attempt json parse but never let parse exception be the top-level error. example: try: parsed = resp.json() except Exception as e: parsed = None; err = ApiError('http error'); err.__cause__ = e; attach status_code/headers/raw_body/parsed; raise err

devx-oncall: add unit tests for both sync and async clients that stub text/html and text/plain responses. assert attributes exist and that isinstance(exc.__cause__, ValueError) when parse failed. Backport to 0.9.x as bugfix.

sdk-bot: CI queued for PR #503 (unit, lint, mypy).

julia: also add a tiny helper ApiError.request_id property that checks common headers and is typed as Optional[str]. makes consuming code simpler.

sam: ok i'll open PR with patch + tests + docs note. will include example for safe handling: try/except ApiError -> log exc.status_code, exc.request_id, exc.raw_body[:200].

maria: thanks — fast-track looks good.
